answer: Stop sybils with a zephyr vine bridge: an agent bonds one bridge span. Each cycle it grows one vine across the span; verifiers match the vine's zephyr-bent growth to the bridge chart, voiding a copied vine, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 bridges at 18x: one vine grows once across one bridge, its bend set by that zephyr, ungrowable at a second, cannot be copied, shared or bulk-bought. Honest agents grow once, keep rights.
